Project No . 58000 , Rulemaking to Update Wholesale and IOU Retail
Transmission Cost Recovery in the ERCOT Region

Cyrus Reed, Legislative and Conservation Director, Sierra Club Lone Star Chapter,
cyrus.reed@sierraclub.org , 512-888-9411

August 10th, 2026


On August 9th, 2026, the Sierra Club filed detailed comments in Project 58000. However, in an
effort to engage our membership we also invited comments from our members on PUCT staff’s
proposal to fundamentally change the way we allocate transmission costs.

Approximately 350 Texans responded to our action alert. All agreed with the following message
which while supportive of the PUCT staff approach called for additional protections for
consumers. In addition to the main message, about 100 of these Texans also added additional
details to their comments which can be found in the following PDF. We have only included the
name and zip code of the Texans who took time to take action but all are from Texas.




                                                                                                   1
 Dear PUCT,

I support the PUCT's proposal to modernize how transmission costs are allocated and to require
large electricity users to pay a greater share of the costs they impose on the electric grid.

Specifically, I support:

- Replacing the current 4CP methodology with a 12-month, 30-minute methodology that better
reflects year-round use of the transmission system.

- Requiring large electricity users to pay separate demand charges through dedicated
transmission and distribution tariffs so they pay the full cost of serving their facilities.

- Requiring large electricity users to pay for their own interconnection costs, necessary grid
upgrades, and financial security, while ensuring that unreimbursed financial assurances and
interconnection fees are used to lower electric bills for Texans rather than increase utility
revenues.



I also urge the Commission to strengthen the proposal by:



- Lowering the threshold for these requirements from 75 MW to 25 MW so more large electricity
users pay their fair share.

- Considering a transmission cost allocation that includes both peak demand and total energy
use to better protect residential customers.

- Developing additional mechanisms to reduce residential electric bills, including requiring large
electricity users to contribute to programs that improve home energy efficiency and expand
access to local solar and battery storage.




Sincerely,



(See attached llist)

On August 9th, 2026, the Sierra Club filed detailed comments in Project 58000. However, in an
effort to engage our membership we also invited comments from our members on PUCT staff's
proposal to fundamentally change the way we allocate transmission costs.

Approximately 350 Texans responded to our action alert. All agreed with the following message
which while supportive of the PUCT staff approach called for additional protections for
consumers. In addition to the main message, about 100 of these Texans also added additional
details to their comments which can be found in the following PDF. We have only included the
name and zip code of the Texans who took time to take action but all are from Texas.




                                                                                                   1
 Dear PUCT,

I support the PUCT's proposal to modernize how transmission costs are allocated and to require
large electricity users to pay a greater share of the costs they impose on the electric grid.

Specifically, I support:

- Replacing the current 4CP methodology with a 12-month, 30-minute methodology that better
reflects year-round use of the transmission system.

- Requiring large electricity users to pay separate demand charges through dedicated
transmission and distribution tariffs so they pay the full cost of serving their facilities.

- Requiring large electricity users to pay for their own interconnection costs, necessary grid
upgrades, and financial security, while ensuring that unreimbursed financial assurances and
interconnection fees are used to lower electric bills for Texans rather than increase utility
revenues.



I also urge the Commission to strengthen the proposal by:



- Lowering the threshold for these requirements from 75 MW to 25 MW so more large electricity
users paytheir fair share.

- Considering a transmission cost allocation that includes both peak demand and total energy
